note: The teachings of Jesus, organized for discipleship. Each item: title, ref, what Jesus taught, and how to live it.

categories.title: The Sermon on the Mount
categories.intro: Jesus' manifesto of kingdom life: not a ladder to climb but a portrait of hearts His grace transforms.

items.title: The Beatitudes
items.teaching: The kingdom belongs to the poor in spirit, the mourners, the meek, the mercy-givers, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, the persecuted — the people the world overlooks are the people God blesses.
items.live: Stop performing strength. Bring your poverty of spirit to God today and receive the kingdom as a gift.

items.title: Salt and Light
items.teaching: Disciples preserve and illuminate the world around them; hidden faith is as useless as flavorless salt.
items.live: Do one good work today visibly enough that someone could glorify your Father because of it.

items.title: Fulfilling the Law
items.teaching: Jesus came not to abolish the Law and Prophets but to fulfill them — every promise lands on Him.
items.live: Read the Old Testament expecting to meet Jesus in it.

items.title: Anger, Lust, and the Heart
items.teaching: Murder begins with contempt; adultery begins with a look. God judges the heart, not just the hands.
items.live: Deal with sin at the root: name the anger or desire you've been feeding, and bring it into the light.

items.title: Love Your Enemies
items.teaching: Anyone can love friends; children of the Father love enemies and pray for persecutors, as He sends sun and rain on all.
items.live: Pray by name, today, for the person who has hurt you most.

items.title: Giving, Praying, Fasting in Secret
items.teaching: Practice righteousness for your Father's eyes, not your audience's applause — He sees in secret and rewards.
items.live: Do one act of generosity this week that no one but God will ever know about.

items.title: The Lord's Prayer
items.teaching: Pray simply: Father, hallowed name, kingdom come, daily bread, forgiven and forgiving, delivered from evil.
items.live: Pray it slowly every morning this week — one line at a time, in your own words.

items.title: Treasures and Anxiety
items.teaching: You cannot serve God and money. Look at the birds, consider the lilies — your Father knows what you need. Seek first the kingdom.
items.live: Name your biggest worry out loud to God, then do today's obedience and leave tomorrow to Him.

items.title: Judging and Asking
items.teaching: Take the log out of your own eye first. Ask, seek, knock — your Father gives good gifts. Do to others what you wish done to you.
items.live: Before correcting anyone this week, confess your own version of the same fault.

items.title: Two Gates, Two Trees, Two Builders
items.teaching: The narrow gate leads to life; trees are known by fruit; and only the one who HEARS these words and DOES them builds on rock.
items.live: Pick one command from this sermon and build it into your week — hearing without doing is sand.

categories.title: Parables of the Kingdom
categories.intro: Stories with a hook: ordinary seeds, coins, and sons that smuggle the kingdom past the defenses of the heart.

items.title: The Sower
items.teaching: The same seed — the word of the kingdom — lands on path, rocks, thorns, and good soil. The difference is the heart that receives it.
items.live: Which soil are you right now? Ask God to pull the thorns of worry and wealth choking His word.

items.title: The Weeds Among Wheat
items.teaching: Good and evil grow together until the harvest; final sorting belongs to the Lord, not to us.
items.live: Release the judgment you've been carrying — be faithful wheat and trust the Harvester.

items.title: Mustard Seed and Leaven
items.teaching: The kingdom starts absurdly small and grows unstoppably large.
items.live: Do not despise small beginnings: one verse, one prayer, one person taught.

items.title: Hidden Treasure and the Pearl
items.teaching: The kingdom is worth everything — the finder sells all he has WITH JOY.
items.live: What are you holding back from God? Compare its worth to the treasure and choose joyfully.

items.title: The Good Samaritan
items.teaching: 'Who is my neighbor?' is the wrong question. Be the neighbor — cross the road, bear the cost, show mercy.
items.live: The interrupted plan, the inconvenient person: that is your Jericho road this week.

items.title: The Lost Sheep, Coin, and Son
items.teaching: Heaven throws parties over found sinners. The father runs, embraces, and restores the prodigal — and pleads with the resentful older brother too.
items.live: Come home if you're far off. Join the feast if you've been sulking in the field.

items.title: The Unforgiving Servant
items.teaching: Forgiven a debt of millions, he choked a man over pennies. Received mercy must become released mercy.
items.live: Name the debt you're still collecting from someone — and cancel it before the sun sets.

items.title: Workers in the Vineyard
items.teaching: The master's generosity offends the math of merit: the last hired receive a full day's grace.
items.live: Stop comparing wages. Celebrate grace given to others as loudly as grace given to you.

items.title: The Rich Fool
items.teaching: Bigger barns cannot store a soul. 'This night your soul is required of you' — be rich toward God.
items.live: Review your actual budget and calendar: are you laying up treasure only for yourself?

items.title: The Great Banquet
items.teaching: The invited made excuses — so the master filled his table from the streets and hedges. The feast WILL be full.
items.live: Who are the 'unlikely' people you could invite toward God's table this month?

items.title: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector
items.teaching: The religious résumé went home unjustified; the man who prayed 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner' went home righteous.
items.live: Trade your résumé prayer for the tax collector's seven words.

items.title: The Talents
items.teaching: The master entrusts his wealth and rewards faithful risk; fear that buries the gift insults the giver.
items.live: Name the gift you've buried — and put it to work for the kingdom this week.

items.title: The Sheep and the Goats
items.teaching: The King counts what was done for the hungry, thirsty, stranger, naked, sick, and prisoner as done for HIM.
items.live: Serve one 'least of these' this week, and know whose face you're actually serving.

categories.title: The Seven 'I AM' Statements
categories.intro: Seven claims that echo the burning bush: Jesus does not merely bring bread, light, and life — He IS them.

items.title: I am the Bread of Life
items.teaching: Whoever comes to Me shall not hunger — He satisfies the appetite beneath every appetite.
items.live: Bring your restlessness to Jesus first today, before you feed it anything else.

items.title: I am the Light of the World
items.teaching: Whoever follows Me will not walk in darkness but have the light of life.
items.live: Bring one hidden thing into His light — darkness loses power when it's named to Him.

items.title: I am the Door
items.teaching: If anyone enters by Me, he will be saved — one door, wide open, into safety and pasture.
items.live: Stop trying to climb in some other way; enter through Christ alone.

items.title: I am the Good Shepherd
items.teaching: The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep — He knows His own by name.
items.live: Listen for the Shepherd's voice in His Word daily; refuse the stranger's voice of shame.

items.title: I am the Resurrection and the Life
items.teaching: Spoken at a tomb: whoever believes in Me, though he die, yet shall he live.
items.live: Speak this verse over your deepest grief — He said it before He wept, and then He called Lazarus out.

items.title: I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life
items.teaching: No one comes to the Father except through Me — the way is not a map but a Person.
items.live: Trade anxiety about the future for trust in the One who IS the way there.

items.title: I am the True Vine
items.teaching: Abide in Me: apart from Me you can do nothing; in Me you bear much fruit.
items.live: Build one daily abiding habit — Word and prayer — and let fruit grow from connection, not straining.

categories.title: Miracles & Signs
categories.intro: Never magic tricks — each miracle is a signpost revealing who Jesus is and what His kingdom restores.

items.title: Water into Wine
items.teaching: The first sign: six stone jars of ceremony become overflowing joy. He saves the best for His hour.
items.live: Invite Jesus into the ordinary places (like a wedding kitchen) — He transforms from the inside.

items.title: Calming the Storm
items.teaching: 'Peace! Be still.' Wind and sea obey Him — and the disciples fear the Calmer more than the storm.
items.live: Say what the disciples learned: He is IN the boat. Name your storm to Him tonight.

items.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
items.teaching: Five loaves, two fish, one boy's lunch — in His hands, enough for everyone with twelve baskets left.
items.live: Offer your 'not enough' to Jesus; He multiplies surrendered lunches, not hoarded feasts.

items.title: Walking on Water
items.teaching: In the fourth watch of the night He comes. Peter sinks when he watches the wind instead of the Word.
items.live: Keep your eyes on Jesus, not the weather. When you sink, His hand is already reaching.

items.title: Healing the Paralytic
items.teaching: 'Son, your sins are forgiven' came BEFORE 'rise and walk' — the deeper paralysis is dealt with first.
items.live: Carry a friend to Jesus like the four rooftop-diggers: pray them into His presence.

items.title: Blind Bartimaeus
items.teaching: The crowd hushed him; he shouted louder: 'Son of David, have mercy on me!' Jesus stopped for one beggar.
items.live: Ignore the voices that say your need embarrasses God. Shout anyway — He stops.

items.title: Raising Lazarus
items.teaching: He wept at the tomb He was about to empty. 'Lazarus, come out' — and death obeyed.
items.live: Jesus feels your grief AND holds authority over its cause. Trust both His tears and His power.

items.title: The Resurrection
items.teaching: The sign of all signs: the tomb is empty, the grave clothes folded, and He ate fish with them. Because He lives, everything He said is true.
items.live: Live this week as if death is defeated — because it is.

categories.title: The Great Commands & Final Words
categories.intro: What Jesus said matters most — the commands He called greatest and the words He chose for last.

items.title: You Must Be Born Again
items.teaching: Religion is not enough — even for Nicodemus. New birth by the Spirit, through believing the lifted-up Son.
items.live: Have you been born again — not improved, but made new? Ask Him tonight.

items.title: The Greatest Commandment
items.teaching: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind; love your neighbor as yourself. Everything hangs on these.
items.live: Audit your day against two loves — not a hundred rules.

items.title: Take Up Your Cross
items.teaching: Deny yourself daily, take up your cross, and follow. Whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.
items.live: Identify today's cross — the costly obedience you've been avoiding — and pick it up.

items.title: A New Commandment
items.teaching: Love one another AS I HAVE LOVED YOU — by this all people will know you are My disciples.
items.live: Wash a foot this week: do the low, unglamorous act of love no one wants to do.

items.title: The Promise of the Helper
items.teaching: It is to your advantage that I go: the Spirit of truth will dwell IN you, teach you, and glorify Christ.
items.live: Stop living like an orphan. Ask the Helper for help — that's His name.

items.title: The High Priestly Prayer
items.teaching: Hours before the cross, Jesus prayed for YOU: for all who would believe through the apostles' word — that they may be one.
items.live: You are inside this prayer. Pursue unity with another believer as Jesus' answered request.

items.title: The Great Commission
items.teaching: All authority is Mine — therefore GO, make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching, and I am with you always.
items.live: Write down the names of your Jerusalem, your Judea, and your ends-of-the-earth. Start with the first name today.
